name: prevent-base-ui-handler
whatItDemonstrates: A favorite (heart) Toggle whose internal toggle logic is suppressed by calling event.preventBaseUIHandler() from a mergeProps-merged custom onClick while the demo is 'locked', so the pressed state only changes once unlocked.
stateManaged: controlled — useState pressed (initially true) wired to Toggle's pressed/onPressedChange via onPressedChange={setPressed}; plus a separate useState locked (initially true) that gates whether prevention applies and drives the Lock/Unlock button label
nonTrivialInteractions: Toggle uses the function form of the render prop: Base UI's generated props are manually merged with a custom onClick via mergeProps<'button'>(props, { onClick }) and spread onto a plain <button>, demonstrating that props are not merged automatically in render functions

the merged custom onClick executes before Base UI's internal handler (rightmost-argument handlers run first) and calls event.preventBaseUIHandler() while locked, so Base UI's internal logic (and thus onPressedChange/setPressed) never runs and the heart stays in its current state
clicking the separate Lock/Unlock button flips locked, re-enabling Base UI's internal logic so clicking the heart toggles pressed
the render callback's state.pressed selects HeartFilledIcon vs HeartOutlineIcon, and the label text shows '(locked)'/'(unlocked)' from the locked state
discrepancies: No tailwind variant exists for this demo; the cssModules implementation is the only variant.
